title: BiCrossNet with Decoupled Dual Generators: A Parameter‑Efficient and Generalizable Few‑Shot Custom Gesture Recognition Framework
claim: A small set of encoder, generator and noise-conditioning modules turns real samples into diverse synthetic embeddings for few-shot augmentation.
layout: 3 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, FiLM-style scale/shift math with ⊙ and +
description: Three horizontally stacked light-blue panels, each with a left-to-right data flow of boxes, trapezoid networks and striped vectors. The top panel, Delta Encoder, takes gesture data samples as a sample pair. A BiCrossNet feature extractor produces Embedding-1 and Embedding-2. These feed an orange delta encoder that outputs a delta vector. A green decoder reconstructs the embedding, and a red dashed training-loss box ties the two ends together. The middle panel, Delta Generator, takes a noise time step through MLPs to a timestep embedding. It then produces scale and shift vectors. Noise is added to the delta vector, then combined with scale and shift through a ⊙ and + operation. The bottom panel, Embedding Generator, repeats this on the embedding itself. Colors code the vector types: green for embeddings, orange for deltas, yellow for shift, gray for the noise step.
caption: Comparison of Workflows between Our Proposed Data Augmentation Methods (Delta Generator and Embedding Generator)
abstract: Gesture interaction and touchless sensing is a natural and intuitive control method that allows users to control devices through natural hand or body movements, reducing reliance on physical input and enhancing convenience and functional efficiency. The biggest challenge is balancing accuracy and model parameter count for custom gesture tasks, while minimizing the number of data samples required for training. This paper proposes a novel IMU-based BiCrossNet model and two novel data augmentation models (delta-generator and embedding-generator) to address this challenge. Compared with existing methods, the model proposed in this article boosts accuracy by 11.7% and 12.7% in UMAHand (public datasets); and 8.85% and 5.25% in GRHand (self-developed datasets), with decreasing 27.8% pretrained feature-extractor model parameters. This research lays a solid foundation for deploying and implementing custome gesture recognition engineering on intelligent terminal devices.
